newsitem.title: FRANCE: Kohl - Euro opponents would lose German elections.
newsitem.headline: Kohl - Euro opponents would lose German elections.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl told French television that German political candidates campaigning against a single European currency in the next election would lose.

" ... I can tell you that anyone who tries to run the next election campaign against the euro, and thus against European unification -- and there are such voices among the Social Democrats -- will lose this election spectacularly," Kohl said in an interview with TF1 television.
A transcript of the interview, scheduled to be broadcast at 1800 GMT, was sent to Reuters.
Kohl said Germans felt a strong attachment to their currency but most felt it was more important to bring Europe together.

"...The great majority of Germans have a certain nostalgia when they talk about abandoning the deutschemark, but they have understood that peace, freedom and togetherness in Europe are more important than anything else," he said.
He emphasised the special role the mark has played in Germany's recent history.

"The deutschemark was there before we even had the Federal Republic, before we had a flag or a national anthem. It was a criterion. When the deutschemark began, most of the gurus -- who were just as dumb then as they are today -- said it would never work. Then the deutschemark became an important currency. Now the Germans are saying, especially to me: 'And now were are supposed to give up the good old deutschemark?'

"And I say along with many other people in Germany, including incidentally the vast majority of German industry which wants the euro -- and that's important: 'I tell you...to build the European house we need a common currency, and that is the euro'," Kohl said.
